01 / THE IDEA

Geometry in motion.
A place in memory.

Two families of spinning circles find a shared point. One gives its horizontal position; the other, its vertical. Together, they trace the shape of a homeland.

f(t) = a₀ + ∑ [aₖ cos(kt) + bₖ sin(kt)]

02 / THE LANGUAGE OF MOTION

The math behind the drawing.

Two real Fourier series, one for each coordinate.

01 / HORIZONTAL POSITION

x(t)=a0+∑k=1N[akcos(kt)+bksin(kt)]

The red circles contribute the horizontal position of the drawing point.

02 / VERTICAL POSITION

y(t)=c0+∑k=1N[ckcos(kt)+dksin(kt)]

The purple circles contribute the vertical position of the drawing point.

Where the coefficients come from

Each integral measures how much of a sine or cosine lives in the border.

ak=1π∫02πx(t)cos(kt)dt
bk=1π∫02πx(t)sin(kt)dt
ck=1π∫02πy(t)cos(kt)dt
dk=1π∫02πy(t)sin(kt)dt
a0=12π∫02πx(t)dt
c0=12π∫02πy(t)dt

a₀ and c₀ give the average positions.

The app evaluates the sampled equivalents with an FFT over 8,192 equally spaced border positions: aₖ = (2/M) ∑ⱼ xⱼ cos(2πkj/M), bₖ = (2/M) ∑ⱼ xⱼ sin(2πkj/M). Replace xⱼ with yⱼ for cₖ and dₖ; M = 8,192 and j = 0,…,M−1.

From a wave to a spinning circle

The same relationship applies to the vertical series using cₖ and dₖ.

akcos(kt)+bksin(kt)=Rkcos(kt−φk)
Rk=ak2+bk2Circle radius / arm length
φk=atan2(bk,ak)Phase offset; X arm starts at −φₖ
kTurns per complete loop

THIS DRAWING, IN NUMBERS

Computing the current series…

Coordinates are centred and scaled to the mainland's height = 1. One loop spans 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π; positive Y points down on the canvas. The Y chain is rotated by π/2 for vertical projection.
